items.title: Roommate turns shared apartment into a yoga studio to make extra money, leaving her roommate unable to use the living room despite paying half the rent: ‘It’s getting annoying'
items.text:
A roommate decided to use their shared living room as a yoga studio three nights a week to make some extra money, leaving the other roommate with no space to use it and no chance to talk about it.

Is it fair to turn a shared living room into a business when your roommate pays half the rent?

Living with a roommate can get complicated when you don't respect the other person's privacy and boundaries. I know how this works because I have one, and we have an awesome relationship. But it wasn't always fun: we had to get to know each other to build a strong bond when it comes to sharing this apartment. Over time, I realized that to have a roommate who's a friend, or at least someone you can get along with, respect is the most important ingredient. Otherwise, it won't work.

If my roommate wanted to make some extra cash by doing some yoga classes at home… I would mind if it got out of control, like it's happening in the story. Three nights a week of paid yoga classes and my living room full of yoga mats like a studio- that's a whole other game because it doesn't let me use the house I'm paying for. It's not fair for the other roommate to deal with that, especially since she's not getting any money out of this.

I'm not saying that the other roommate has to share the money, but some consideration would be nice. I don't think she realizes how much space she's using for her yoga classes, and how much it forces the other roommate to stay locked in her room because she can't get out… Sometimes having a business doesn't align with living with a roommate.

items.title: 25+ World Series Memes for Wisconsinites Celebrating the Milwaukee Brewers First World Championship (October 29, 2026)
items.text:
There's something so special about a team who has been chasing the highest-level of victory for years on end finally doing it. Every single fan that has been loyal to the Brewers since the team was founded in 1970 has wanted one thing, and all of them got it last night.

If you've never been a fan of a team who has never won anything, you don't know the struggle of showing up year after year and watching your team lose. While it can be miserable to be a fan of a team that seems destined to lose everything forever, it really does build character. It teaches you to be loyal to your hometown, even when your hometown is pretty mediocre. It facilitates community, whether that is with your family or friends. If your team is bad enough to have $6 tickets throughout the entire regular season, you can have so much fun and misery all in one summer.

As someone who grew up near the Brewers, I'm happy that they won! My family would drive up there to go to Twins and Cubs games, and my sister and I would always get really excited when Bernie Brewer would slide down his slide. My parents really tried to explain to us that we shouldn't be excited when that happened, because that meant that the team we were rooting against got a point, but we couldn't help it! I love mascots who do wild stunts, and I always will.

There is also something to be said about the value of small-market teams finally winning it all. New York and LA already have so much going for them in the world of sports. They both have two MLB teams for crying out loud! They've both won so much, and the system is rigged for them because they have more money. In smaller cities without Hollywood or Broadway, sports are the most important cultural institutions they've got. When everyone in one city is united for one team, it's a beautiful thing to be a part of. If you called off work today to celebrate the Brewers long awaited victory, these World Series memes can be a part of your celebration.

items.title: ‘Level too Hard, Baba is Done, Better Look Out’: 13 Baba Is You Memes for the Intellectual Gamers
items.text:
Baba Is You: Like Solving Equations (Except It's Not Boring!)

I've been playing Baba Is You. For those who don't know it, it's a puzzle game that feels a little like solving equations, except they are made of words.

It seems really simple at first, but as you level up, you will likely find yourself stuck thinking really hard about how to solve the challenge.

The premise is simple: you control a little character named Baba that looks like a mouse or a capybara, and the rules of the game are written right there on the screen, like blocks of text that go: BABA IS YOU, WALL IS STOP, FLAG IS WIN. Those aren't only instructions about how the game works; they are buttons you can actually interact with.

If you move the words around and you form new phrases, you actually change what the rules of the game are.

For example, if the wall is closer to you, and you change the command from WALL IS STOP to WALL IS WIN, pushing the words around with Baba, and then you touch the flag using Baba again, you will win.

I know it sounds very simple, but it turns very complicated very fast.

The relationships between words and equivalences, and rules, are what remind me of equations. Language becomes both the problem and the way to solve it. Just like when you have an equation and you move numbers around and suddenly you clear x. Numbers were presented as a problem, and through some operations they became the solution.

I'm not sure I'm explaining my theory right, but that's how I feel about the game. Contrary to what people might think, it's very relaxing. Even though you're thinking most of the time, it's a different kind of thinking, and it gets you so concentrated that you forget your real-life problems completely.

Don't get me wrong, please; it doesn't feel like math homework. Please try it before making any assumptions. There is something so satisfying about solving a problem without looking at solutions and playing around with logic without feeling like we're back at school. At least that's the kind of game I love.

Baba Is You reminds me of Monkey Island, in the sense that you spend a lot of time looking for new combinations of stuff to get new results. It's not about doing it fast or dexterity; it's about logic and creativity.

Does anyone else in here like these kinds of games as well? I would describe them as games that stimulate your creative thinking and require you to constantly evolve your way of thinking about problems.

Anyway, I have to keep playing because even though I loved it, I haven't reached a super high level or anything. That's my new goal in life lol.

So, for those who already know and love Baba Is You, here is a compilation of memes to remember it fondly and to try to tempt you into going back to play it.

items.title: Family takes in a kitten from a feral colony to foster, but her bond with their son and Great Danes changes everything
items.text:
Fostering a kitten is supposed to be temporary. You give them a warm place to sleep, plenty of food, and lots of love until they're ready for their forever home. Unfortunately, nobody told little Agatha that she was only supposed to be staying for a few weeks.

When one family took in the tiny kitten, the plan was simple. Agatha had come from a feral cat colony and needed someone who could bottle-feed her and give her a safe place to grow. The family had fostered plenty of kittens before, so this wasn't exactly unfamiliar territory.

But there's a big difference between fostering an entire litter and caring for one tiny kitten. With a litter, the kittens have each other to play with and cuddle. When there's only one, you end up spending much more time holding, feeding, and bonding with them. That's a dangerous situation for anyone hoping to avoid another permanent pet.

Agatha also had some pretty convincing allies. The family's son took on overnight feeding and cleaning shifts, sometimes caring for her between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. All that time together paid off, and the little kitten grew to absolutely adore and trust him. Looking at their pictures together, it's pretty clear the feeling is mutual.

She even managed to win over the family's Great Danes, joining them for afternoon naps. Considering how tiny Agatha is next to those enormous dogs, we can only imagine how comfortable she must be snuggled up beside them.

But the moment that really sealed the deal involved the family's husband. About two weeks after Agatha arrived, she was crying for her bottle when her foster mom heard him coming down the hallway, reassuring the kitten that Daddy was coming to get her.

Well, that's one way to announce you've become a cat dad.

By that point, it sounds like Agatha had already made herself at home. Between her devoted human brother, her giant canine cuddle buddies, and a dad who was completely wrapped around her tiny paw, there wasn't much reason for her to go anywhere else.

Now approximately nine weeks old, Agatha has officially graduated from foster kitten to permanent family member. The little former feral kitten has traded life outdoors for the comforts of being a thoroughly spoiled house princess.

Should you have to tip on something you didn't get service for?

Tipping culture has gotten way out of hand these days. It's a pretty huge part of living life in 2026. We're adding 20 percent to everything we do, and that's just the way it goes. But does this mean we have to stand for it? Tipping on something that you didn't even get service for is a pretty big ask. You have to wonder, who is it even going to? Tipping is important to do for workers who rely on it for their income. This was me for a long time. If the tips weren't coming in, then I was in the hole. And it's frustrating for everyone when that's the case. It passes the buck from the owners to the customers in a way that can feel unfair. If we all just made a living wage, then we wouldn't have to worry about it, but that doesn't seem to be the case these days. It's also frustrating for a customer, though, because you don't want to have to pay extra for something you didn't even receive. Not these days. items.title: ‘Me at 11 PM After Eating Healthy All Day’: 17 Gym Memes for the Gym Bros Who Can’t Stop Eating Junk Food
items.text:
I Skipped the Gym for an Entire Week for the First Time in 10 Months. When does wanting to improve yourself become an inability to accept yourself as you are?

And suddenly it doesn't matter that I've been going consistently for a year and a half, that I always eat perfectly, or that even when I think I ate too much, I probably only ate 200 extra calories.

I know our bodies aren't supposed to be machines running at maximum capacity every day, but every time I miss a workout, the tiny voice in my head drives me crazy with questions.

For the past week or so, I haven't felt like going to the gym; that's it. It feels like a big deal in my mind, but it is really only that. I can't believe it has gotten to the point that if I skip a workout, I feel that I'm going to lose what I built over a year of working out. And if, on top of all that, I've been eating more carbohydrates, you can only imagine how I feel.

After this terrible experience, I've decided I'm not going to push myself this hard, and that I will give myself permission to stop and recharge when I need to. After all, I've proved myself time and time again that I'm not a quitter; there is no reason to worry that much.

Habits are built over time, and skipping the gym for a week doesn't suddenly erase the 500 weeks prior when you showed up. What began as an attempt to improve my quality of life can become another scenario where you scrutinize yourself, and that wasn't the point.

If rest is no longer rest, and it has become a pause from constant productivity: congratulations, you've succesfully trapped yourself. My new gym objective is that being active is just another thing that I do because I enjoy it and not something I constantly obsess about and that it runs my life.

Consistency is not the same as perfection. If I intend to do this for the rest of my life, I have to be able to accept some degree of ups and downs. I would like to reach the point in which I no longer stress about it, like I don't stress about taking showers or eating; it's just something that I do and that I will continue to do (hopefully) forever.

I will probably go back to the gym soon, when I feel ready, and I suppose I'm going to feel ready as soon as I stop treating the issue like a court summons. Until then, I will eat what my body tells me to eat, and if later this week I need to detox, I'm going to do it, but I will resist the urge to compensate for what I'm doing now.

The point of getting healthier was to enjoy life, not to find another way to suffer or feel guilty. Has any of you had this issue as well? Any tips to get over it?

items.title: Fifth grader goes to a Halloween event and surprises his parent with a kitten instead of candy
items.text:
Kids have a talent for bringing home unexpected treasures. Rocks, sticks, mysterious objects they found on the playground, and occasionally something that probably should have stayed outside. Parents learn pretty quickly to check their children's pockets before doing laundry, because you never know what might be hiding in there.

A live kitten, however, is a pretty impressive addition to the collection.

Most parents expect to come home from a school Halloween event with a bag of candy, a few decorations, and a child who's had way too much sugar. Bringing home an entirely new family member probably wasn't on the schedule. But when a kid spots an adorable kitten who needs a home, good luck convincing them to walk away.

We have to admire the confidence of children who decide they're getting a pet without consulting anyone. They don't worry about litter boxes, vet appointments, or introducing a new animal to the family cat. They see a tiny furball, fall in love, and figure the grown-ups can handle the paperwork.

One parent recently experienced exactly this situation while helping out at their fifth grader's elementary school trunk-or-treat event. They were busy running a trunk when their son discovered a nearby house giving away kittens. Rather than asking permission, he simply picked one out and brought her over.

His parent was understandably stunned. It had started raining, though, and they couldn't bring themselves to return the little kitten to the house. They already had a seven-year-old cat at home, so caring for a feline wasn't completely unfamiliar territory.

The kitten appeared to be around five weeks old, much younger than the age kittens should normally leave their mothers. Her new caretaker knew she needed extra attention and immediately made a trip to PetSmart for supplies.

They bought kitten food, kitten milk replacer, a litter box, bedding, and other essentials before setting her up in a separate bathroom away from the resident cat. The little one was dirty and had fleas, so they carefully cleaned her with a warm washcloth and flea comb while arranging a vet visit for the following morning.

Although the family hasn't decided whether they'll keep her permanently, they're determined to give her the care she needs. Her unexpected arrival has certainly made this Halloween a memorable one.

That fifth grader might have gone looking for candy, but he came home with something considerably sweeter.

However, having a holiday specifically for them also feels right. When you lose your soul pet, you lose a part of yourself, and you are never the same again. You now carry a pain with you that is always in the back of your mind and weighing your heart down a little bit more. However, this pain is also a reminder of the love. And wow, what a love to have forever with you! The connection between a human and their beloved pet is something else. It is worth the pain you have to hold after they pass. So let's celebrate our furbabies the way they would have wanted us to: with joy and laughter. Any pet parent knows your pets absolutely LOVED to make you laugh.

items.title: Young man calls savings accounts 'dystopian,' questions why a 24-year-old with $5K wouldn't use that money to go to New York Fashion Week: 'It's more dystopian to not have savings.'
items.text:
It's pretty common for 24-year-olds to have nothing in savings. In fact, most 24-year-olds have a negative net worth from student loans or credit card debt, so any 24-year-old who has a positive net worth is something to celebrate. There is definitely such a thing as "living in the moment" too much, and if you willingly spend every penny you have on fun things, you're not going to be in a good position when you need your money for necessities.

There was a time in my life when I spent nearly every penny I made. I did always make sure to save a percentage of my income into my 401K, but that was easy! After all, it came directly out of my paycheck, and I didn't even have to think about it. But from ages 22 to 24, I basically spent all the money I made on whatever I wanted: Broadway tickets, basketball games, Citi Bike day passes, you name it! I just made sure I never let my bank account drop below a certain amount, so I wasn't spending more than I made, and that was good enough for me at the time!

As I've grown older, I've recognized the importance of saving more for my future. It's not enough to just save 10% of your check for retirement! You need an emergency fund of 3-6 months to cover unexpected expenses. You need to invest in the stock market so your money grows instead of sitting in a regular savings account forever. If you want to go on vacation, set up a "sinking fund" so you can save specifically for that, instead of draining your retirement account to go to a resort.

While some people are serious about saving money in their 20s, many aren't, even into their 30s, 40s, and 50s. Some adults with great jobs and kids still don't have $5,000 to their name, even though they make double that every month. When people have a high income but no savings, it points to a pattern of being undisciplined. If you can't delay pleasure and you buy everything you see, it's not a good sign for your long-term financial health.

It is pretty darn common for 24-year-olds to spend every dollar they have. The young man in this story is probably around that age, and he's learning that most people aren't as willing to spend their life savings as he is.

items.title: The 20 Best Friendship Memes of The Week
items.text:
I love my friends. They are the only people I can stand for more than two hours.

Friendships are one of the purest forms of love, and I stand on that hill. I always viewed friendship as the love that someone has for you even though they don't have to. Family is obliged to love you, and even then it's not always possible to accomplish. But friends don't. They don't owe you anything; they choose to love you. And to me, that is the purest way of love. So don't undermine your friends; they are people who choose to be by your side and want you to be the best person you can be.

At weddings, it is common for people who are close to the couple to say some words about them. I always like it when they move the family to the side for a little bit and let the friends talk. It doesn't matter if it's a childhood friend, a work friend, or someone you met two years ago in an elevator and became inseparable. They always have the most beautiful view of their friends. It's a vision that is untainted with expectations or family links. It's the view that shows that no matter what, they are there for each other, not because they have to, but because they really want to. And to me, that seems to have come out of a fairy tale. Yes, the mother of the bride knows her like the palm of her hand because she raised her and lived with her for years. But the friends learned everything about them by spending time together, and now they have noticed the little things that make the bride the person that she is.

Friendship is beautiful and pure, but it can also be toxic and tumultuous. But you know what? When your friendship is like that, it is because they aren't really your friend. When we were children, nobody taught us how to spot the people who want to take advantage of you or use you for something. On the contrary, we learn to always expect the best in people. Well, that wasn't really helpful. I'm not telling you that you need to be second-guessing everything and always assuming the worst, but you do need to trust your gut and be intelligent. If your "friend" is always trying to take you down or make you feel bad, then that isn't a true friendship; that is a toxic relationship that will only work to make you feel bad about yourself. You need to realize that and leave. We all deserve a friend who is nice and wants us to be the best version of ourselves, not someone who is praying for our downfall. So think about who your real friends are and prioritize them over others. They choose to be your friends because they love you, not because they want something in return. So be mindful and smart, and don't ever stay where you are not wanted for who you are.

items.title: Business owner lets customers park in neighbor's driveway, gets annoyed when he starts charging $10 for parking: 'I'd asked him to stop several times'
items.text:
Nothing is bound to cause a rift between neighbors like vehicles not being parked where they should be.

It is a concept that is so simple, yet apparently so hard to grasp for so many people who live near others: you should only be parking your car on your own property, or another place where you have express permission to do so. It is an unfortunate truth that the average home only has so much space for vehicles, but that is a problem that you have to work out for yourself if you end up with more cars than driveway space.

Millions across the country rely on their cars as their main form of transportation. It is no surprise that any block in their ability to drive and store their vehicles comfortably is going to feel like a major issue. Even if they don't have a car at all, it is very presumptuous for somebody to use their neighbor's property without even getting the proper permission.

Things get really ugly when the person dealing with this transgression tries to find a way to fix it. If somebody thinks that this is OK to do, they are likely to take issue with any attempt to stop it, no matter how mild. This can often be a situation in which subtlety is not your friend, and strong action needs to be taken. Sending the right message is half of the battle when neighbors are not willing to respect the normal boundaries.

items.title: Framer's Extra-Small Chihuahua Named “Tiny” Herds Animals Just As Well, If Not Better Than Any Other Shepherding Dog Breed
items.text:
What kind of dogs were bred for breeding? Every dog was bred by us humans for some sort of helpful purpose. Great Pyrenees are livestock guards, Dachshunds were bred to hunt those tiny little burrowing creatures, and Border Collies were bred to herd livestock. So what were chihuahuas bred for? Their purpose goes so much deeper than tasks needed for manual labor.

Chihuahuas were bred before modern society was even a glimmer in humanity's eyes. Back in Mesopotamian civilizations, they bred Chihuahuas for spiritual, ceremonial, and companion roles. items.title: 10 Halloween Costume Ideas for Couples
items.text:
Halloween is just around the corner, and you still haven't decided on a costume to do as a couple? You are lucky I got some ideas!

As I love Halloween, I am the perfect person to suggest costume ideas. Especially because this year I wanted to dress up with my boyfriend, and until we found something that worked for us, we reviewed every possible option. That's why I will present you with the 10 best and easiest costume ideas to do with someone else. And I will also tell you what I'm going as; maybe you can copy me if that's more your style.

The easiest costume ideas that I found for couples were definitely Joe and Love from the show You. It's especially easy. You just need one person dressed in an apron and holding a rolling pin, and the other dressed in black with a cap, and if you want to do it creepier, you can both splash yourselves with some red paint. It's easy to do, easy to understand, and easy to clean after. You don't need any crazy things, so it's also really cheap. Another good idea that is easy is Nick and Judy from Zootopia; it's a little cliché, I will admit. But that doesn't mean that it isn't good. You can either pick stuff from your closet and make it work by adding the ears and a tail, or you can buy a costume online, which is also pretty inexpensive.

If you can manage to do something a little bit more complicated, I would suggest doing Coraline and Wybie from Coraline. It's not that hard; the main things are the wig and the button eyes, but I get that wigs aren't for everyone. And if you are feeling like painting your whole body, I would really like to see at least one couple dress as Beast Boy and Raven from Teen Titans. It's so cool and not really that impossible. You just need to commit to the bit and paint yourself. It's not that bad.

I left more ideas below, but just in case you are curious about what I'm wearing to Halloween, I will be dressed as Misa Amane from Death Note, and, of course, my boyfriend will be dressed as Light Yagami. Yes, I know what you may be thinking: that isn't a love story, and I know. I just found the characters really interesting, and I thought it would be original to be dressed like them. After all, the idea of Halloween isn't for the costume to be perfect. It's more important to have fun with your friends or your partner and enjoy the scariest night of the year. Halloween is great whether you are dressed like a trash bag or as some great horror movie character. You just need to have the time of your life, and that is not dependent on your costume attire.

items.title: ‘The Memes Strike Back’: Star Wars memes for Rebels, Imperials and Force Users to Laugh at Across the Galaxy (October 28, 2026)

Imagine what it must have been like for Luke to stand up to both Darth Vader and Palpatine, given that he wasn't even alive when the Jedi Order still existed and never knew how they operated as a whole. If he had had another experienced Jedi by his side, the rebellion would have breathed a little more easily. Besides, by that time almost everyone seemed to have forgotten about the Jedi. Han Solo kept looking at Luke as if he were insane!

You could argue that Ahsoka and Kanan, who were still alive, weren't really Jedi. Ahsoka had left the Order, and Kanan never got to officially finish his training before starting to train Ezra, but at least they had seen how the original Jedi operated. Luke never did. Yoda did what he could to train Luke, and he did a good job, but still. Yoda was a great master, and Luke had it in his genes to be a good pupil, but it's not the same to have some training in a skill you had barely known existed and then off to save the world as it is to have more experienced people by your side to accompany you and give more insight. Still, Luke managed, and we love him for it.

items.title: Meowhere to Hide From Clingy Kitties Who Want to Be Wherever Their Hoomans Are
items.text:
Cats have a reputation for being independent, but some of them missed that memo. These clingy little furballs can't stand being more than two feet away from their favorite humans, and they'll make sure everyone knows it. Forget having a moment to yourself when you've got a furry shadow following your every move.

Anyone who lives with a velcro cat knows that purrsonal space is pretty much nonexistent. Going to the bathroom? Your cat is coming along. Trying to cook dinner? There's a feline supervisor weaving between your ankles. Want to sit on the couch for five minutes? Congratulations, you've just volunteered to become a heated cat bed.

Don't even think about closing a door. To a clingy kitty, a closed door is a personal insult that requires immediate action. They'll scratch, meow, and shove their paws underneath until you finally surrender. You could be gone for thirty seconds, but judging by their reaction, you'd think you'd abandoned them for several years.

Working from home is another adventure when your cat insists on being involved in absolutely everything. They'll sprawl across your keyboard, block your computer screen, and demand head scratches during important meetings. Your boss might be expecting that report by Friday, but your cat has decided it's time for mandatory cuddles. Answering emails can wait until your feline supervisor is satisfied.

Some of these cats can be incredibly picky about affection, too. They'll spend twenty minutes screaming because you're not paying attention to them, only to walk away the second you actually try to pet them. Cuddles are only acceptable when they're the ones making the rules.

It's hard to stay annoyed when your cat curls up against you and starts purring like a little motor. Sure, you might lose all feeling in your legs because you don't have the heart to move them, but that's a sacrifice most cat parents are willing to make. Being chosen as your cat's favorite person is a pretty big honor, even if it comes with absolutely no privacy.

These affectionate little kitties have taken the phrase attached at the hip to a whole new level. Whether they're following their humans from room to room or demanding cuddles at the worst possible moment, they've made one thing perfectly clear.

Once you've got a velcro cat, you're stuck with them furever!

items.title: Fragrantica Scent Notes: 18 Moments 'olfactifications' Using the 2000s Layout of the Perfume Encyclopedia Website
items.text:
Nostalgia can create the smell of a memory that doesn't exist and put it in the iconic Fragrantica layout

Fragrantica Notes or the Fragrantica Trend, also known as the Fragrantica Meme, is a series of exploitable memes using the 2000s layout for the perfume encyclopedia website Fragrantica's scent notes tool, which tells users the notes they might smell in a given perfume.

Some things we never lived, but we can picture how they would smell. Some other things seem like we've all strangely been through, and we can all recall how the happiest day of summer as kids smelled.

Some people online have designed the most perfect smells that would instantly transport us to the deepest, most specific memories and points in our lives, or perhaps in the lives of other imagined beings who lived what we never dared to.

Smell can be a very quick way of being transported to other scenarios. If you think about it, only one smell can take you to a country, to a point in history, to the house of someone you love, almost imediately.

You have to be very sensitive and delicate to be able to decode what composes a very peculiar smell, and how to tell a story through it. I guess that's what people who work as noses do. The trend originated on TikTok and populated the rest of the internet from there.

None of these notes have to be objectively correct; fragrance, just like art, is not an exact science. It's vocabulary for creating an atmosphere. One that's particularly left out of most artistic works. There is no smell in movies, paintings, or music, and it's just as powerful when it comes to creating atmospheres and evoking feelings.

I like smell because it creates a three-dimensional experience; one can close their eyes and feel transported. I'd love to see more artists exploring smell. We already have playlists for every conceivable mood, movies for every taste, and food for every palate. I want to have commercial perfumes that evoke a specific character or the smell of rain in Minnesota.

I met a girl online a few weeks ago who gets together with a group of people to review fragrances, and they often go to places where they create niche fragrances and try them and all. I asked her to invite me to their next meeting, and I've been super excited about it.

The last one got cancelled because the group decided that the place they had rented for the meeting had 'too many smells coming from the streets' and that would interrupt our 'smelling session'. I thought it was hilarious, but it made me even more curious to see how seriously they were taking the whole thing. As soon as I go, I'm going to write about it.

Perhaps smell can become another way to experience art, a profoundly meditative one, because it requires closing your eyes and connecting to the present moment very vividly.

Have you ever smelled something and felt 15 years younger for a second? Can anyone imagine what a very fond memory smells like? An objectively bad smell, like a musty bedroom smell, can still evoke a beautiful memory from our childhood?

items.title: ‘You’ll Get Hurt if You Mess With Me’: 10 Funny Kero Frames to Remember the Gluttonous Guardian
items.text:
For those who love and miss Kero every day, or those who wish they had a small, intelligent, winged guardian following them around all the time

I'm not usually a fan of anime, but Sakura Card Captor definitely occupied a place in my heart as a child. It catered to my most basic childhood wishes: that my cat could talk and that I was a beautiful superhero saving the world.

I fell in love with Kero from the moment I first saw him, and now, revisiting the show to write about him, I realize I still am, and that I was always attracted to the same type of personalities in characters.

Last week I wrote about Salem; a few days ago I wrote about Jake the Dog, and today I'm writing about Kero. It seems I love cute little creatures who happen to have infinite wisdom, sarcastic humour, and a tendency toward self-centeredness. It might be because I see myself reflected in them? Who knows.

Kero's full name is Keroberos. He is supposed to be a guardian beast, but clearly, his figure doesn't suggest that. He was entrusted to help Sakura protect the Clow Cards, yet he spends most of his time gaming, worried about food or cranky about something.

I think Kero's archetype is something like the wise fool. He proves that being smart doesn't have to be solemn. His authority doesn't prevent him from being funny or childish at times. He can be both, and one doesn't erase the other. I think this is a beautiful way to look at intelligence, and in my opinion, it's how it naturally presents itself. We have this idea that very intelligent people should be serious, put together, or very mature at all times, and in reality, that couldn't be further from the truth.

What I also love about characters like Kero is that their affection is not portrayed through sentimentality; he shows his love through actions. He is not endlessly gentle or openly sentimental.

He teases Sakura, disagrees with her, and complains about her, but he still loves her in his heart. He does this because they're intimate, and they know and love each other very much, just like we do with our loved ones.

He, just like Salem and Jake, uses his humor to shield himself from vulnerability, and also to communicate with Sakura. Jokes create a shared language, and sarcasm can be a way to show affection without exposing one's vulnerability too much. I find this completely endearing.

I also love the contradiction between him being a magical being while also being a gamer and a junk-food lover. He is not a character to admire, and he is not a role model; he is a character to have fun with, and to remind us that life is about those simple pleasures too.

Not everything has to be about protecting the Clow cards or saving the world; some things can be about cakes and gaming till midnight.

Give it up for Kero!

items.title: Financially struggling mom considers banning child and spouse from Christmas when they complain about dollar store gifts: 'We have almost lost our house several times'

Christmas isn't just about the gifts.

It has long been observed that the festive period has become more about spending money and consuming as much as possible, but that isn't the only reason that people observe the Christmas holiday. Even those who are not invested in the spiritual part of it can get behind the messages of spending time with loved ones while spreading kindness and good cheer. People get so sidetracked by ongoing arguments and petty drama that they end up ruining what should be a happy memory. It makes this time of year one that many dread for this reason.

Gift-giving has long been an important part of Christmas, but arguably, it is sometimes a little materialistic to cling to it as the most important part of the holiday as an adult. It is still possible to have a good day with family even if there isn't all that much money to spend on each other. Didn't A Christmas Carol try to tell us about this? It is almost always nice to receive some presents, but that shouldn't be what is at the center of festivities. The more important thing is appreciating the effort that has been taken to see each other and enjoy each other's company.

items.title: Mother demands that her neighbor close his curtains when watching TV so her kid won't see through them, instead of teaching her child not to spy on the neighbors
items.text:
A kid from the neighborhood was looking inside a neighbor's window while he was watching American Horror Story, so the mother went and demanded that the neighbor watch kid-friendly shows or close his curtains instead of teaching her kid not to invade people's privacy.

What is it lately with parents and blaming other people for their own kids misbehaving?

Seems like parents are tired of parenting lately, and instead of actually raising their children to be respectful human beings ready to live among society, they let them run wild and then confront and antagonize other adults who try to set a boundary on the child. Because children need boundaries. They can't just be left to do whatever they want or cave to their every whim. That's when you get disrespectful kids who throw temper tantrums over nothing, and the parent just stands there, looking into the void while the kid makes a mess around them.

I know a handful of people who are good neighbors and friends, but when it comes to parenting, they are not the best. Their kids do nothing other than nearly crawl up the walls and run around enclosed spaces while screaming and nearly making everyone around them trip and fall to the floor. They have almost made me fall a couple of times. And let's just say that they don't take it very well when you tell those kids to stop and behave correctly.

Truth is, it's their job to raise them, not everybody else's. They can choose to ignore their parenting tasks if they want to, but they certainly have no moral authority to come to anyone else and tell them how to live their lives, especially because they're incapable of controlling their own kids.

items.title: Parents criticize Paris Hilton for dressing as Belle and dressing her 2-year-old daughter as a teacup in their 'Beauty and the Beast' family costume
items.text:
Was she trying to take the spotlight away from her little girl? Or is this standard Paris Hilton behavior we should expect by now?

It's common for families to do coordinated group Halloween costumes and post them on social media. I first remember seeing it from Neil Patrick Harris and his family, and the trend has trickled down from celebrities to normal families. Even though the trend started years ago, celebrities still do it, including Paris Hilton and her family, who dressed up as characters from Beauty and the Beast. Paris dressed up as Belle and dressed her daughter up as Chip the teacup, which enraged some parents and amused some of her fans.

items.title: The 20 Best Phrases Said by Lorelai Gilmore
items.text:
Gilmore Girls: the TV show that best evokes the feelings of the autumn season and has one of the best satirical line deliveries.

I love Gilmore Girls. It's easily one of my favorite shows that was ever created. Every time I'm sad or gloomy because of seasonal melancholia, I always rewatch it to feel better. The whole idea of sitting on the couch to watch this series gives me an autumn vibe. I feel like I need to be eating a cinnamon roll with a pumpkin spice latte or a hot coffee. But this show is not only cozy and calm, but it's also really funny. You may get into the series at first thinking it's just another mother-daughter story in a small town with curious characters, but it's much more than that. It's witty, hilarious, intriguing, and very satirical. The line delivery is perfect, always talking at a fast pace with a lot of sarcasm and pop culture references that are great for someone with such a love for it like me.

Lorelai Gilmore is the mother of the show, a once teen mom who decided to care for her baby on her own even though she was just 16 years old. She was from an upper-class family with a lot of money, but she left everything and worked hard to get to be independant and the only provider for her child. Funny enough, this child's name is also Lorelai, but everyone calls her Rory. She is a very clever girl with big plans for her future that include going to Hardavrd to be a journalist. She takes enormous pleasure in reading, especially classics, which is shown multiple times on the show and has even created lists online with all the books she reads through the whole series. The story starts when Rory gets accepted into Chilton, a private school that will help her get into Harvard, but it's extremely expensive. To pay for it, Lorelai decides to ask her parents — with whom she doesn't have a good relationship — for a loan. They accept, but they have to come every Friday for dinner with Rory. This is the beginning of all the craziness that is about to come in the show.

My favorite part of the show has always been the way the characters are portrayed, the journey they go through, which proves that none of them are perfect or the worst. They are human; they make mistakes, but they all have a kind heart and big dreams. The difference is who got to accomplish them, and whose life is very different from what they had planned for themselves. The way the show is articulated is also very interesting. The phrases are memorable to this day, and some references are still relevant even now. That's why I made a compilation of my 20 favorite Lorelai phrases so we can all be the judge of how good they actually are. To set the mood, I will tell you that my all-time favorite was always "Oy with the poodles already".

items.title: October's 24 Most Creative Halloween Costumes for Moms to-Be This Halloween

Do you know what is spookier than spooky season? Parenthood. It doesn't matter how much you prepare for it, it's filled with unexpected twists and turns. items.title: Friends bail on Airbnb 3 days before trip, demand $800 back from nonrefundable charge and are baffled when friend refuses: 'They say I am stealing their money'
items.text:
If you've ever arranged an Airbnb for your friends, you know how much of a commitment it can be.

There are pluses and minuses to being the friend who is good at planning. I'm that person, so I know allll about it. I'm naturally the person who wants to take control of plans and make sure that everything is in place. I'm booking the stuff and making the plans. I try not to overexert myself and truly commandeer the trip or activity or whatever it is, but somebody needs to book the Airbnb. And that somebody is going to be me. There are some good things about being this kind of person. You're ultimately in control of what kind of experience you're going to have. You're helping set the parameters of how much you're going to spend and what kind of place you're going to book. Plus, I happen to love researching Airbnbs. It's one of my pastimes. But there are a bunch of drawbacks to being this kind of person. The main one is exactly what happened in this story. If you're the one booking, then you're the one putting your card down. You're happy to get the credit card points, but you have to chase people down to pay you back. If you have friends who are weird about money, they might get weird about paying you back. This is never a fun position to be in with the people you love. You don't want to feel like they owe you money, and they don't want to feel like they owe you money. And if something goes wrong in the friendship or during the trip, you might be on the line for hundreds of dollars you weren't expecting to be. It's never a good idea to mix money and friendship, but sometimes you have to if you're going on a trip or having an experience somewhere. That's what happened here, and what unfolded set a weird chill over the friendship.

items.title: Cat Sibling Memes for a Meowjestic Meme Competition With Your Sibling
items.text:
Have you punched and hugged your sibling today? Yes, preferably both at the same time.

Growing up with a sibling is growing up with a friend. A friend that is constantly overstepping their boundaries and talking to your parents too much when you also happened to do something wrong, but a friend, after all. To be fair, you probably told on them as payback a couple of times too.

A sibling is always someone you can count on. For example, you can count on them to enter your room and steal your clothes, or eat the last piece of cake you saved all week, even though it clearly had your name on the box.  You can also count on them to get the human version of the "zoomies" if they ever find you sitting comfortably on the couch, trying to have a break (how dare you). You can count on them not letting that happen. Also, spoiling the show you just started to watch and changing the password to Netflix when they get slightly angry at you.

This collection has the perfect cat memes for you to send to your siblings, trying to get them to apologize for every time they disrupted your peace with an uncalled-for and random attack. Alternatively, to remind them that you still need to behave like an unbreakable family unit when mom comes back ready to scream at someone. In other words, no matter how many times you fight, loyalty must prevail. And, of course, amazing cat memes can do the trick.

items.title: Mother gets accused by her in-laws of eating the candy that was for her daughter, she gets offended and gives back all the food: 'Now you don't have to worry about me, my husband, or my daughter eating anything you purchased'
items.text:
Why would your in-laws think their daughter- in-law is eating the candy they are gifting their grandchild? Do they not trust her to keep the food for her? Can't the kid share her treats with her family?

Some in-laws are very weird towards their daughters-in-law. As if they couldn't accept the person that their child married just because they are not biologically family. This always makes me think if the problem is whether they don't trust their child's ability to choose a decent and loving partner, or if it's just because it's an outsider to the family and they need to act defensively. Whatever the case is, it's not only malicious to be acting this way, especially if they are the mother of your grandchild. They are part of the family whether the in-laws like it or not, so it's better to get used to it instead of acting all weird and crazy. They married into your family; they didn't steal your child or push it away from you. They just fell in love and decided to form a family on their own. Isn't it easier to accept them into your family than to mistreat them all the time?

The grandparents in this story are not doing things right. They are being incredibly disrespectful by assuming that a mother would take a gift that was supposed to be for her daughter. Yes, it's just candy, but it's also so much more than that. If a mother takes candy from her daughter so she can eat it, what other wicked things does she do? The saying "taking candy from a baby" is the most well-known phrase to describe a witch, so do they think the mother is a witch? I think that these in-laws are either overthinking some little situation and creating a huge mess over it when it's nothing in reality, or they just saw the kid offer one of her candies to her mother and they took it the wrong way — which is insane to do.

I don't like this people's attitude, and I do think that if they do this big of a mess over something this dumb, then it's better to keep your distance from them. If this whole family drama started over some candy, what can happen with a bigger misunderstanding? I don't think that they like the mother of their grandchild in the first place; the way they acted all defensive over nothing proves it. I do think that the mother is right to be upset over this. After all, they are spreading lies about her, and even if they are dumb, no one wants people to be lying about them, especially to their family. I do hope that the husband stands up for her family and either makes his parents understand why they are wrong or at least forces them to change their attitude. No one deserves to be treated like this, and taking your distance seems like the best solution to avoid a bigger fight over nothing.

items.title: 22 PlayStation Memes for Gamers Who Finally Have Money for Games but No Time to Play Them
items.text:
Can I add a free afternoon to my cart along with the game?

When I was little, my mom got my brother and me a PlayStation 2 and our lives changed forever. Can we agree that the PS2 was the best PlayStation ever??? I admit that nostalgia is influencing my judgment. That console gave us so many afternoons of fun that I don't mind being a little biased. Ours was modded, which meant it could play copied discs, which meant we could play thousands and thousands of games! The games cost next to nothing, so we ended up with a lot of games. There was always something else to try. Choosing a game didn't have to be a major financial decision like these days.

One of the games I liked the most was SingStar Pop (and we played it with the microphones!). items.title: DCU Memes for All DC Comics Fans Who Are Begging James Gunn to Deliver a Good Justice League Movie and Choose the Right Batman
items.text:
You can never please everybody, and anyone in the entertainment industry sure knows that better than anybody…

If you're like me, every time you set foot on the internet and see people complaining about stuff, specifically entertainment-related stuff, you wonder: What does it take to please an audience? Because, so far, not even movie directors have figured that out, especially not movie directors working on superhero projects.

After the release of Clayface, director James Gunn is defending his work, expressing the idea that not all stories within the same universe have to lead to the same outcome, and people on Twitter don't quite seem to agree with him, for whatever reason they have.

Gunn's work for his DCU has been compared since the beginning with Zack Snyder's vision for his own, and there are always mixed reactions. Some people praise him for having more variety of tone across the shows and movies of this new universe; others are happy that now the productions seem to have colors besides grey, and others believe Snyder's universe was more complex and better plotted. Some people thrash Gunn's movies and call them 'awful', asking that he be fired, saying that he's not a good director, and so on. However, if you look at the numbers, you'll see that his version of Superman has an 83% critics' acceptance on Rotten Tomatoes, and 90% from the audience. Lanterns has a 91% from the critics and a 67% from the people; Supergirl is the lowest, with a 52% from the critics, but a good 72% from fans. And so far, Clayface has been doing great, with a 75% from critics and a 94% from audiences.

If the general reception is good and reviews are positive, why are people so critical? Well, that has an easy answer: people like complaining. And that goes to show that whatever mean comments go online are not necessarily a reflection of what happens in reality. Numbers rarely lie, and if DC is keeping James Gunn in their projects, he must be doing something right.

items.title: 25 ‘Anne With an E’ Romantical Memes to Share With Your Kindred Spirits
items.text:
"It's delightful when your imaginations come true, isn't it?" I would love for my 4th season imaginations to come true, no doubt.

I found Anne with an E scrolling through my Netflix profile one day. It was a quiet afternoon, and I was looking for something silly to watch. The kind of content you can sleep through. Of course, those of you out there who have watched the show know exactly what I was jumping into. I never expected to be so invested in a group of people living in a place with the name "Green Gables", but here I am. items.title: Press Start to Laugh With These Hilarious Video Games Memes for RPG Fans Who Have Been on the Same Side Quest for Three Hours

items.title: 'He's twice the size of my other Sphynx cats': Couple adopts an 11-year-old giant Peterbald cat after his owners can no longer care for him, and he fills their house with hilarious chaos
items.text:
Babe, wake up, new cat just dropped.

Here, at ICHC, we pride ourselves on being cat expurrts. All of us writers have been here for years at this point. There is not a single piece of internet cat news that we have missed. The new cat breed that was discovered? We were on that. There is not a single cat meme that has evaded us. Heck, some of our own handmade memes have gotten attention online. Every cat vet emergency is something that we've seen before. Except when it comes to our cats, who make us panic when they do anything slightly off.

We know cats. Exept that apparently, we don't know them well enough. Somehow, after years of working in the cat field, today, we were caught off guard. We thought we had seen all the unique and rare cats that existed already. The Maine Coons, the Cornish Rex, the common orange… because oranges are all special in their own ways. But we were wrong. And we're so happy about that. A new cat discovered is always something to celebrate. And if that cat is a hilarious, chaotic menace… then all the better.

You'll see what we mean.

items.title: Tiny black leopard is born to rescued parents who survived a terrible past, and when his mom can't raise him, humans step in to give him a life full of love
items.text:
Our parents always try to give us the best life that they can. This leopard couple succeeded in doing it for their baby.

I think that this is something that every child can relate to. At some point in our lives, we become aware of our parents' finances. We get a deeper understanding of how they grew up, what their childhood looked like, and all the ways that they tried to make our lives better. We realize which things we took for granted that we shouldn't have. It's a little mind-blowing. Suddenly, we're a lot more thankful for everything that they have given us than we were before - all the ways that they worked so hard to make our lives better. That desire, of course, is true for all parents, not just humans. Felines are the same.

This desire to make life for our kids better is why stray cats sometimes bring their babies to the humans that they trust. It's why cats co-parent, taking care of babies from different litters together. And we're sure that the leopards in today's story, all 13 who were living in captivity, were trying to make life for their babies better in the same way. They simply couldn't - because of the conditions they lived in. Bad humans are everywhere. But so are good ones. And when the good ones came to rescue these 13 leopards, 2 of them were about to have a baby.

They lived in captivity, but their cub was born into a life full of love. And that's what all parents want for their babies.

items.title: 'Which TV series has a 10/10 unskippable theme song?': Fans discuss what is the best theme from a TV show that is so good they never skip it
items.text:
Fans of TV shows gathered to discuss a matter of utter importance: What is the superior theme song of a show?

Theme songs are a very important part of TV shows. If it's that good, it will be stuck in the brain of the viewers as they grow old. It will add a lot of sentimental value to the show. Writing a perfect theme song isn't some code you crack or a mathematical problem you solve. A lot of what goes into it is simple luck. It needs to be a catchy song, but not annoying. It needs to have good rhythm, but also blend well and be cohesive with the style of the show. It needs to be memorable. The thread is full of different examples of what fans believe is the best theme song, but I have my own thoughts on the matter.

My favorite theme songs from TV shows are, in no particular order: The Simpsons. I'm not sure whether it's because the song is really good or more of a case of nostalgia. Every time I hear the first The Simpsons… chant, I'm back to being a 10-year-old kid obsessed with the show that was waiting all day for dinner time to get to watch it while I ate. Another incredible one is the Anne with an E theme song. It's an example of a song that perfectly captures the essence of the TV show while also working as an incredible song on its own. The real title is "Ahead by a Century" by the Canadian rock band The Tragically Hip. Another theme song that is very dear to my heart is the one from Gilmore Girls, "Where You Lead I Will Follow". It's a perfect way to describe the bond the mother and daughter, Lorelai and Rory, have, but it's also a song that works great on its own outside of the show.

If you ask the people in your circle what song they believe is the best theme song of all time from a show, they will most likely say the one from Friends. It has that magic that only the music from TV has. It's timeless, extremely popular, and super iconic, I must say. I may not consider the show one of my favorites, but the song is definitely in my top five. Another one that is also very popular, and it's the best one according to the fandom of this show, is the one from Game of Thrones. The only way I can describe it is as if you were getting teleported to the world that they portrayed by just listening to the first chords. There are a lot of amazing theme songs, but they all have one thing in common: they are all still stuck in our brains even though so much time has passed since we last watched these shows. They are a very important part of every series, and they can take you back in time when you hear them.

items.title: 'Chauffeurs or private drivers for ultra wealthy/powerful people, what's something you've overheard that you'll never forget?': Drivers for famous and wealthy people spill the tea about things they have overheard during their job
items.text:
Being a limo driver or a fancy car chauffeur for wealthy people and celebrities can definitely make you hear gossip.

Famous people and celebrities are a big interest of mine; some people like to pretend they don't care about that, so I'm all for knowing about the life of the Kardashian family, reality shows, and celebrity weddings. I love all that. I find so much joy from hearing celebs gossip; the lifestyle of the rich and famous is actually a good way to take my mind off of things that worry me, to dissociate. That's why I like watching reality shows and reading about royal weddings. It's a dumb interest, but it surely helps to forget, at least for a while, about other things that are going on.

This thread made me think about when people reveal stories about their interactions with famous people. They usually have two ways of going: they say they were super nice and they were able to take a picture with them, or they were incredibly mean and it completely changed the perception they had of them. These kinds of reactions always led me to think that it may be that the celebrity could be having a bad day, or wanting to avoid pictures, and by just denying whatever request the fan had, now they are incredibly mean and do not deserve the fame they have. It could also be that they are lazy or entitled and don't want to take pictures with people they deem less important than them. As if they wanted the fame but not the tasks that come with it. We would never be fully sure a famous individual's behavior is entitled and mean or a sweetheart unless we are the ones who meet them in person, and even if we do, they could just be having a bad day or simply not like the attitude that you had when approaching them.

So, do we believe these stories that "fans" tell about the celebrities they have encountered? That is completely up to you; you can believe it, consider it simple gossip, or defend your favorite celebrity through everything. You are entitled to your own opinion about them. But I do think that judging someone's character according to one encounter that someone had may be biased. But if you hear the same story over and over again about one particular celebrity always acting entitled and mistreating everyone, then well, you do have more reasons to believe that it isn't simple gossip. But, again, we cannot know for sure, as we haven't met them yet. I like simply reading about those encounters that people had and take them like that, just a good story; whether it's true or not, it doesn't affect me in any way. And even if they are in fact entitled and annoying, that is not really that relevant to me. I may like celebrity gossip as a distraction, but I do not care whether they are nice or not in real life.

items.title: Miami apartment dweller reveals the biggest downside of living in a high-rise: 'I was successfully deinfluenced'
items.text:
Skyscrapers may be glamorous, but they sure can be inconvenient as well.

Tall buildings have become an unavoidable part of every major city skyline in the past century and a half, to the point that it is kind of weird to imagine urban life without them. It's hard to believe nowadays, but the building that is commonly considered to be the very first skyscraper was only 10 stories tall. Things have only gone upwards from there on out.

Although they seem to be a fact of life at this point, it is important to remember that living or working that close to the clouds is a very recent development in human history. As a result, we don't exactly have all the creases ironed out yet. There are plenty of horror stories about very tall, unbelievably expensive buildings that simply haven't been designed that well. Think 432 Park Avenue in New York, where residents have sued due to severe defects like excessive swaying, structural failures, and an explosively loud garbage chute. Then there's the case of 20 Fenchurch Street, otherwise known as the Walkie-Talkie, in London, which had to be redesigned after it reflected sunlight so strongly that it damaged cars and caused fires.

In short, there is usually a price to pay if engineers and architects do not thoroughly think through the logistics of making such big and impressive buildings a reality. Those who pay the price for that are the ones who use them every day and quickly figure out what they could have done better.
