My character is Kai, an Aasimar barbarian. She's not an ooga-booga tribesperson from the forest - she's just an 18-year-old with a lot of pent-up rage and teenage angst. She's at a very low point in her life right now, and I'm excited to see where it leads her once she's on the other side. I can't believe I'm finally going to play her again tomorrow!

items.title: 'I could smell smoke in my house': Resident yells at neighbor to move his grill during a party, later apologizes for his unneighborly behavior
items.text:
We all do and say things when we're mad that we end up regretting…

It's so easy to let our anger take the wheel and lead us to some actions we are not proud of. It's hard to see or think clearly when something is making our lives uncomfortable or inconvenient, especially when that something was caused by other people. We get mad when someone holds up the line, or when a party down the street wakes up the kids. The question is: are we able to control the anger, or do we let it take over and lead us down unwanted paths?

Everyone would love to claim that they are the masters of their own emotions, that they don't lose rationality and let anger take control, but we all fall victim to those feelings every once in a while. It's only human. We get mad at strangers, friends, and even family members, and we say or do things we later regret. That happens, and we learn to make peace with it, but it is also important to try to make peace with people we might have offended in the process. There's nothing wrong with recognizing you crossed the line and apologizing for doing so.

The resident in the story below realized he might have reacted too strongly to an honest mistake, so he tried to make things right. It all started when he woke up in the morning to a smell of smoke in his house and realized it was coming from the neighboring backyard. When he saw his neighbor out there cooking on his grill, he got mad and demanded that the neighbor move the grill further away. The neighbor quietly complied, but the resident didn't feel much better afterwards.

As the day went by, the resident felt like his reaction to the grill was too strong, as the last thing he wanted was to be perceived as an entitled or mean neighbor who no one wants to talk to. This led him to the peace offering he gave his neighbor, which then led to a lovely afternoon for the two households. Everyone loves a wholesome ending, so scroll down to read the full tale.

items.title: 20 Weather Memes for This Autumn That Doesn’t Feel Like an Autumn Yet
items.text:
Autumn? Did it start or…

I hate the feeling when a season changes, but it still feels like it didn't. If the season changed, then I expect the first day of said season to feel the correct temperature. If it's autumn, then why haven't I yet seen yellow, brown, and green tree leaves on the ground; why haven't I felt the temperature a little chilly; why isn't it raining every five seconds? From the 21st, I'm always expecting to feel like the season is supposed to feel; I hate having to wait days for the weather to actually change. That said, I also hate when it's supposed to be a season, and it starts feeling like another one. For example, those days in summer when suddenly it's really chilly outside, and I have to change the bikini top for a hoodie. If it's summer, then it's hot out, not a mixture of all seasons the whole year. I like my seasons feeling like the correct one, with the correct weather for it.

Autumn is a particularly nice season; some would say that it's the best one —I'm some people. It's nice to go out with a coat but not be extremely chilly, to eat hot cocoa or coffee but not get frozen on the way out, to watch series while trapped inside a blanket, but not needing to turn on the heater. Is the chilly, not-so-chilly weather; it's the best of both worlds. I have certain traditions when it comes to autumn. I like to wear more earthy colors in my clothes, to have more coffee than usual, and, of course, watch Gilmore Girls. That TV show is autumn made into a series. I like feeling like I'm one of them, as if I were actually Lorelai Gilmore, drinking my hot coffee at a dinner while living in a town that organizes events for the people. It's the dream life of every book girly who loves autumn. So now, get your book, your blanket, and a hot beverage, and enjoy this weather. Enjoy the autumness of this season; I can promise you you will miss it when it's gone.

items.title: The Best Halloween Episodes in Sitcoms
items.text:
Halloween time is so good it even has its own episodes.

It's October, which means it's officially Halloween time. Yes, I know we still have a whole month before the celebration starts, but Halloween isn't just another festivity; it is my—and a lot of people's—favorite holiday. That's why it deserves a whole month of celebration and preparation. If you don't have any plans before the 31st to start preparing yourself for all the spookiness, or if you are too afraid of horror movies, then you need to watch the different sitcoms' Halloween episodes. This thread made a lot of series fans get invested in deciding which show had the best Halloween episode.

If you asked me, I would say that The Simpsons: The Treehouse of Horror is a no-miss. Almost every single one of them is spectacularly made, mixing the spookiness of the season while still being funny and upbeat. My favorite one is definitely the first one that ever aired: "Treehouse of Horror", season 2 episode 3. It has a parody of The Raven, the poem by Edgar Allan Poe, and it has the first-ever appearance of the aliens, Kang and Kodos. It's a must-watch from the series.

One other special that is very dear to my heart because of how unhinged and hilarious it is is one from the sitcom Community; to be specific is season 2, episode 6, and it's called "Epidemiology". In this episode, there is a Halloween party at the community college where everyone starts to feel really bad and turns into zombies after eating the cheap food that Dean Pelton bought from an army supply store. It makes the whole school get locked up in a study room till they all become zombies. It's witty, it's hilarious, and whoever wrote it is definitely insane. But what do you think? Which is the best sitcom Halloween episode and why? There's definitely a lot to pick from. What do you think about the others' opinions? Are they on to something or just blinded by the love for the show?

items.title: ‘Yippie Kayak, Other Buckets’: 25 Brooklyn 99 Memes to Get on Captain Holt’s Good Side
items.text:
"Um, did something awkward happen? I can probably relate."

If you ever feel bad at your job, don't forget that in some alternate reality there's a police station in Brooklyn that keeps giving Hitchcock and Scully cases to solve. Let's face it, those cases are as good as gone. Probably lost in the black hole that is Scully's desk drawer. So, you're good.

The best and worst police station has given us some of the most memorable laughter moments in TV history, and today, we have brought you a collection of memes to honour the original police dream team. Also, it's the perfect occasion to bring back some of Boyle's most iconic wisdom moments and family traditions. My favourite? "Piece of advice: Just give up. It's the Boyle way. It's why our family crest is a white flag." Words to live by in adulthood.

If you're ever in need of a brilliant group of police officers to keep you safe and bring justice to your life, maybe don't rush to the 99 station. You'll be lucky to get on Amy's to-do list, but there's also a big chance that Gina will keep you on hold for the rest of the week. That said, if what you're looking for is true bliss and happiness, get your cool, cool, cool on and tune in to Jake Peralta's journey to get Captain Holt to accept him as a lost son.

Brooklyn 99 has got it all. Suspense, detective investigation, a heroic team, a rogue main character, and an office competition to determine which bakery makes the best apple pie. You know, the most important things for good law enforcement. Also, let's not forget the upcoming Halloween heist. Instead of doing silly work reports, you'd better start preparing to win the grand prize and become the ultimate human/genius.

Some things stay in our hearts forever: friendships, significant others, family members, and one of the best sitcoms of all time. As they say, one always returns to where one was happy, and what a fortune that place happens to be the same place of work as the one and only Rosa Diaz. Yes, she might look like she could hunt you down to the ends of the earth just because you slightly made fun of her look, but at heart we all know she's a sweetheart.

items.title: 22 of the Best Marvel Cosplays Giving Us Inspiration for Our Spooky Season Costumes
items.text:
I need all my cosplayers out there to show up and bring it all on for this Halloween!

Cosplayers have my utmost respect. What they do is a whole different kind of art. It doesn't take just imagination, but also a lot of skill. Most costumes you see at Comic-Con or other events are really well thought out and planned with at least a few months of preparation. It's not just choosing a character and then sewing a little dress that kind of looks like what they wear. Nope, it's a whole lot more than that. Many costumes involve complex makeup, wigs, props, and the outfit itself takes time, money, and effort. Most cosplays have so many details that if you pass by them too quickly, you might miss them. They are not the kind of costumes you can buy anywhere; they are the kind you need to know how to draw a specific sewing pattern, have a lot of skill to put it together, and adjust it to the body so it almost looks painted on you.

Seeing any cosplay is a sight to behold, but I'm personally biased to like Marvel and Star Wars cosplays, and yes, also anything Disney-related. With Disney, it might be a little difficult because you're mostly dealing with 2-dimensional characters, so bringing them to real life takes a whole lot of adjustments. With Star Wars and Marvel (or any superhero cosplay, for that matter), the issue is different. Many of the original suits are supposed to be high-technology, modernized armor, or combat gear. How do you replicate that with fabric, plastic, cardboard, and foam rubber? Well, that's where the skill and experience come in to do what they do best: transform random materials into a movie-worthy costume!

Even if most of us mere mortals don't have the time, skill, or resources to pull it off, we can still be inspired by these awesome people! Even more now that Halloween is so close and we seriously need to up our game and find a costume that makes us shine. Here you have 22 of the best Marvel recreations out there to start diving into the cosplay world and preparing for your next costume party!

items.title: 27 Grool Mean Girls Memes That Definitely Go Here, Especially on October 3rd
items.text:
It's not a Wednesday, but I'm wearing pink for this batch of Mean Girls memes.

Mean Girls… how do I even begin to explain Mean Girls? I haven't seen this movie in a very long time. I'm talking years. The first time I saw it was around 2004-2005, when a friend from class borrowed the videotape at Blockbuster (Boo, you old!) and we watched it at her house. I can't even begin to describe what a canonical event it was in my life. This is when I stopped wanting to hang out with cooler mean girls in school and embraced my nerdiness completely. Like, I got in a loser, and stayed a loser. And I loved every second of it.

I probably watched it a couple more times in my teenage years, and that's probably it. That's just how it used to be back when you didn't have everything ready to stream at the press of a play button. This generation doesn't understand that the limit does not exist for them. But in the 2000s, life was simpler, and honestly - that's what made movies like Mean Girls iconic. No need for an Avengers multiverse produced with a budget of eleventy bajillion. Just a simple idea, awesome delivery, and a grool script.

Some people watch Mean Girls religiously every October 3rd, and I totally get them. But I'm a testimony and a living piece of evidence that you don't need to watch it like you're obsessed with it to remember every line, love every character, appreciate every joke, and be a true fan. So much so that if this movie punched you in the face, you'd think it's awesome.

items.title: 'She told me I was "erasing" her son's identity': New mom demands that everyone call newborn by his elaborate full name, considers limiting contact with 30-year-old brother for using nickname
items.text:
My mother and I share the same first name. So, when I was born, in order to distinguish between us, she insisted that everyone call me by my first and middle name combined. This was all well until I learned to talk, and I had trouble pronouncing my name. The mispronunciation of my name became my lifelong nickname, and my extended family still calls me by it whenever I visit.

But today, we're talking about a new mom similarly insists that her family members call her son by his first and middle name – and last name, too! For whatever reason, she wants to hear his full legal name whenever he is being referred to. The baby's uncle refuses to adhere to his sister's request, but he later finds out that this may come at the expense of his relationship with his nephew. As if family wasn't complicated enough, now people are adding demanding rules about how relatives are supposed to call their nieces and nephews or else they'll get cancelled. Cancel culture really has gone too far.

Everybody with a "complicated" family knows how difficult it can be. Our parents grew up in a different time than we did, and their parents treated them very differently than our parents treated us. Views on discipline changed. Views on expression changed. The world changed. But sometimes, it's hard for our parents to let go of what was incorrectly taught to them, causing situations like this to happen. Arguments like this come from fear, maybe it's a fear of holding onto something or fear of letting go. But no matter what, fear is not a good reason to make a decision. The first step is recognizing this, and then, true change can begin.

items.title: Dad goes through 15-year-old son’s phone and finds out he has a PS5 at his mom’s house, he demands son bring it to his so his 6 stepsiblings can play too, son refuses: 'It’s going to get broken with 6 kids running around'
items.text:
I grew up playing video games religiously. It started with a small PlayStation, then a GameCube. After that, we got a PS2, and we didn't get anymore consoles, but I didn't mind. I was so drawn to the GameCube and all the games it provided. My favorites were different versions of The Sims, all the Mario Party games, Super Smash Bros Melee, and many more. As an adult, I still love to play video games, and sometimes still wish I had my GameCube. I can totally understand the appeal of buying the latest edition of gaming consoles and games. These days, video games are quite literally an art form. From the plot and levels, to the animation, the soundtrack, and everything else involved, it's like an extremely sophisticated immersive experience.

Especially as a young boy, video games are your escape from the real world. You can leave all your worries behind and immerse yourself into a fantasy world where you command earth-shattering spells, you can fly on the backs of a pegasus or grow your own wings, slay dragons with your own hand, or steal riches without a single soul noticing. Sure, there are many multiplayer games that are fun to share, but it's often something you do to retreat and recuperate. Especially if you have a turbulent family life. And perhaps even six stepsiblings you didn't ask for.

This leads us to our topic today - a teenage boy who has a PS5. His parents are divorced and his mother is better off than his dad. His mom bought him the PS5, so he gets to play every week he's at his mom's place. His father finds out and demands he share his PS5 with his stepsiblings, but the son refuses. You can only imagine where this is going.

items.title: Daughter swears not to take care of parents in their old age after they refuse to forgive her for leaving med school to follow her passion: 'I told them flat out that won't be happening'
items.text:
Every parent loves imagining what their kids will be like when they grow up, and they all want their children to end up happy, successful, and stable. However, some parents their take musings over their kids' lives way too far and let them become expectations. They plan their kids' futures meticulously, ignoring their wants, needs, and dreams. If these parents' sons and daughters stray from the path laid out before them, they risk facing family disappointment, and in some cases, being completely shunned by the very people that are supposed to support them the most.

Just like most parents, ours wanted us to be a successful businesswoman, doctor, or lawyer. And we tried to be interested in those things, but we just love writing. It called to us from an early age, always journaling and documenting life around us. It's what brought us joy, and when our parents saw how happy we were when we were writing, they couldn't expect us to do anything else. Because, in the end, our parents wanted us to be happy. You would think most parents would react that way, you might hope, at least. But that's unfortunately not the case.

In our story today, a woman decides mid-med school that she wants to pursue a career in design. Her parents, who banked on her becoming a doctor, take the news really harshly. However, when they see her succeed in her field years later, they begin to talk about more expectations that they have for her. Not forgetting how they treated her as she struggled to make it as a designer, she outright refuses. Scroll down below to get all the details.

items.title: 29 Motherhood Memes That Nail the Chaotic Joys of Raising Tiny Humans
items.text:
Each day feels like some sick joke, where you never get proper rest, proper nutrition, and no one even appreciates all the effort you put in. Date night with the hubby turns into watching half an episode on Netflix before bed, and Saturdays are filled with endless laundry. It's not an easy feat, and even though your kids don't appreciate it from you now, they will as you get older.

Being a new mom can take the years off of you, but it's only temporary. When the kids are grown, and the hubby is the breadwinner, you'll be able to relax in style. You'll get back into your pilates, your keto diet, and your skincare routine. And don't forget that date nights will come back again; from movie nights to going to bars like you did when you were younger. It may seem like lightyears away, but the only way to get there is with some laughter at the tenacity. What better way to laugh than to scroll through memes about parenting? At least they understand your pain.

items.title: 32-year-old husband lies to wife about finances, has secretly been stocking funds into a private account with more than $45k, wife goes back on their agreements for finances and childcare
items.text:
Sacrificing yourself to a relationship and someone else is one of the hardest, most vulnerable things to do. Finding out you've been lied to, tricked, duped, or deceived is so viscerally uncomfortable. No one wants to feel like they've given themselves to the wrong person. It can create so many trust issues along the way that it makes sense how hesitant people are to really get into a relationship at all. The story here is about a married couple. They had an agreement throughout their whole marriage about finances and childcare. They just had a daughter, and their agreement was that she won't be in daycare because of a trauma on the husband's side.

They're trying to narrow down options for their health insurance, when the wife gets a call from the DHHS. They inform her of what they're eligible for, but in the process, she finds out her husband is making a lot more than he's telling her. She finds out he's been adding money to a private account he kept hidden from her.

items.title: Adopted 17-year-old finds out parent's have secret college fund for golden child little sister but not for him, he confronts them about it but they dismiss him: 'It's none of your business'
items.text:
Being adopted is a complicated issue for many. Even if you have the best parents out there who really wanted to have kids when they adopted you, the world around you may make you feel like you're lesser, unimportant, or unloved compared to bio kids. In the story here, there's a lot going on. The protagonist is a 17-year-old boy who was adopted. His parents were with him during his bio mom's birth, so the connection is deep. But three years into having him, the couple gets pregnant biologically with a girl. So now he has a little sister who he perceives as the golden child. They worship her, they baby her, she gets all the cuddles, love and nicknames while he feels like he's treated as a second class son.

As he gets older, he finds out that his parents have a college fund for his golden child little sister but not for him. He confronts them about it, but doesn't get the closure he wants.

items.title: 'We're never moving to Virginia': New York couple refuses to move to mother-in-law's hometown when wife is pregnant, she guilt trips them about being closer to her grandson
items.text:
The world is a big place. Everything in life is location, location, location. We would all be completely different people if we were born somewhere else, grew up somewhere else, or moved somewhere else now. Though we all see the same sun, moon, and sky, it can feel like we're breathing different air and living in alternate universes based on where we are. In the story here, location really is everything. The couple met in college, she's from New York, and he's from Virginia. They've been together and living in New York for ten years and now they're pregnant with their first child.

It's Thanksgiving dinner, and they're at the husband's family's home for the holiday. His mom is going on and on about how she would love for them to be closer, and now that they're pregnant she laments how sad she'll be to not see him growing up. It's a harsh truth but the verisimilitude of the situation is that the couple has no intention of moving from New York. The wife tells her MIL straight out how it's never going to happen.

items.title: 25 Introvert Memes That Accurately Depict the Desire to be Alone
items.text:
Whether you're man, woman, child, or animal, we all can be introverted. There's something about modern day culture and society, the rise of technology, that allows us to be introverted guilt free. Unlike the days without cell phones, we had less of an excuse to cancel plans, to say no to the hang out, or to prefer your alone time. Nowadays, alone time is crucial and usually what we all love to do with our rest time is something with technology. Whether it's scrolling on Instagram, watching videos on YouTube, a show, or a movie, we love to just sit back and relax in front of a screen. Sure, there are some of us left out there who prefer a good book to anything else, but that doesn't make them more or less introverted.

Introverted comes from the feeling that we recharge from social situations by being alone. The joy of looking forward to not opening your mouth to talk, not having to hear someone's voice talking to you, not having to look someone in the eye, not having to feel anyone else's energy.

items.title: Flashback to the 90s With These Iconic Memes That Tickle Our Nostalgia Bone
items.text:
There's way too much I miss about growing up in the 90s and early 2000s. Kids these days will never understand the beauty of phoneless hangouts, not knowing what time it was with friends till the twilight hours of the morning, not worrying about what you look like because there wasn't the potential of a camera taking your photo at any time, and the general lack of aesthetic competition that comes with growing up today. Our childhoods were filled with borderline inappropriate, yet genius cartoons, self deprecating humor, existential dread, and knowing how to ride a bike or use a map.

Our natural instincts and human skillsets are dwindling as the generations go by. Where our grandma's were baking homemade bread and milking cows, we can barely heat up our microwave pot put properly without burning our uncalloused little hands. These days, kids growing up can't even write with a pen and paper because their hand cramps too easily. I have some words for those kids: my hand cramps from texting and typing! See how it feels to be an old millennial looking to the past.

items.title: Woman calls out sister-in-law for fake allergy at Thanksgiving dinner, she demands to go home early but husband makes them stay for dinner, causing family dispute
items.text:
We all know that one person who just randomly made up an allergy one day for attention. That's not to say allergies or food intolerances don't exist, because they very clearly do. But there are people who claim things that we all know aren't true. This is exactly what happens in the story below. The protagonist hosts Thanksgiving dinner every year because of her spacious apartment, every year she makes the same things. This year, however, her sister-in-law sees her cooking and has a freak out over the mushrooms in the stuffing, claiming she's allergic and has always been allergic. It's not so much that she's allergic, but her reaction to seeing mushrooms is a bit intense and over the top to begin with.

After hearing this, the protagonist asks her how long this has been going on and when she found out about the allergy. The SIL claims she's always had it, to which the protagonist bursts out laughing since she's been putting mushrooms in the stuffing every single year.

items.title: 'You're a spoiled brat': 38-year-old woman kicks out boyfriend after he calls her 8-year-old daughter spoiled for leaving a plate on the table, the internet encourages her to leave the relationship
items.text:
Dating is hard enough, but it becomes improvidently harder when you enter the dating arena with children already. In the story below, the narrator is a woman who's dating a man, both in their 30s and both with children from a previous relationship. They've never seen eye to eye on parenting, and it's becoming more and more of a divider in their relationship. She has an 8-year-old daughter, and he has a 4-year-old son. The daughter is starving for a father figure, and she tries to be affectionate with him and hold his hand, but he refuses.

He feels uncomfortable doing it since he's not her real father. He seems to be a bit harsh with her, to his girlfriend's disagreement. She wants him to be more of a father figure to her. But the real icing on the cake hits when her daughter leaves a plate on the dinner table, and her boyfriend tells her that she's a spoiled brat. It's bit extreme for a child, and she has every right to question him.

items.title: Woman refuses to spend Christmas with her in-laws after MIL treats her poorly, husband threatens divorce and their marriage is on the line: 'You're being selfish'
items.text:
Christmas time isn't all fun and joyous celebrations full of love. It's a stressful time that could bring unsettled tensions to the forefront. All the family gets together, and suddenly that thing that happened four years ago comes out and you realize you're still resentful. In the story below, the protagonist is a woman who's fed up with her in-laws. She has always had tension with her mother-in-law, and this year for Christmas she just wants to relax. Usually, they go to her in-laws place, and she ends up doing a lot of cooking and cleaning while there. Her and her husband decided that they'll just spend Christmas together alone with their son, and even get an Airbnb so that she wouldn't have to work at all.

Her husband decides to change their original plans of the Airbnb, and go to his parent's anyway. She protests and claims she doesn't want to go. He becomes enraged and even threatens divorce. The comments are all telling her it's a red flag, but read the full story below to see for yourself.

items.title: Woman shares secret family recipe for "married women only" with 50-year-old cousin-in-law who plans to remain single, family explodes at her for breaking tradition: 'The cousin didn't "earn" it'
items.text:
Every family has that one thing that they take a little too seriously. For some, it's the annual holiday card photo. For others, it's the seating chart at Thanksgiving. My own family is incredibly intense about learning a new coordinated dance for every cousin's wedding. Then, there's families that guard their family recipes like they're nuclear codes, even if all they really amount to is tomatoes and the same old herbs.

One such household is at the center of today's tale; they're really protective over their recipes. And they're not just interested in keeping the cooking information within the family; they are very particular about the marriage status of those in the know. One woman marries into this family and is consequently endowed with the classified knowledge of how to make their red pasta sauce. However, she causes quite the stir when she shares the recipe with her spouse's cousin, a woman in her 50s who was born into the family but never got to learn how to make the dish simply because she isn't married and doesn't plan to be.

items.title: 'We won't be in touch': 30-year-old tells roommate he's never going to speak to him when they move out, causing tension at home
items.text:
Roommates are difficult. They can really make or break your quality of life. There's nothing better than coming home to good roommates who you enjoy, who you can talk to about your troubles, who you can have a social life with from the comfort of your home. But when you come home to bad roommates and feel like you have to make a direct run for your bedroom upon entering, then you know you have a problem.

In the story below, the protagonist has been living with his roommate for a few years, which is a long time to live with someone. He claims they have no communication. When his roommate casually drops that in 5 years they won't live together, but will still keep in touch, the protagonist immediately gets heated and informs him that there's no way they'd be in touch. This causes unnecessary tension between them. Read the full story below.

items.title: Woman gets fired on the spot for getting entitled coworker arrested for stealing her $1800 ergonomic office chair: 'He refused. So I called the cops'
items.text:
If you spend most of your day sitting at work, it's important to have a comfortable chair. Anyone who's ever worked a desk job know that a bad one can ruin your spine, mood, and will to live by 2 p.m. That level of comfort isn't always guaranteed by chairs bought on company coin, however. One new hire decided to buy her own $1800 ergonomic chair for her job and accidentally ignited a workplace war.

Theft in the workplace isn't anything new, but it certainly doesn't make it right. Most of the time, it's desk supplies or lunches in the communcal fridge that go missing or end up where they shouldn't be. But in today's tale, it's the aforementioned chair. When this new hire comes to work one day, she finds her coworker parked in the personal chair that she bought with her own money. He refuses to move, and management barely paid attention to the matter. So, our narrator decided to call the police and press charges right on the spot. She might have also gotten fired for escalating so much, but at least she got her chair back.

items.title: Parent excludes son's wife from kayaking trip because she can't swim, she takes it personally despite valid safety concerns: 'If she learns how to swim, she can come next year'
items.text:
Every family has their preferred ways of spending time together. Some love competitive board game nights or cozy movie nights. My own family bonds primarily through the enjoyment of food; from making our favorite recipes to trying out new restaurants, eating is a foolproof way for everyone enjoys themselves and each other. There are families out there, though, that love to go on adventures. Whether it's a yearly road trip or an annual winter getaway, the adventurous types tend to be quite cautious in their vacation safety prep, which is pretty important since nature doesn't really care about sentimentality and rarely makes exceptions.

Not everyone accustomed to the great outdoors is really aware of how dangerous it can be, however. When one parent enforced a long-standing safety rule— that no one is allowed on the annual intensive kayaking trip unless they know how to swim—tension rose fast. The son wanted to bring his wife along, despite the fact that she's never learned to swim. The parents told her if she took lessons, she might be able to come along next year, but this year, she's out.

items.title: Entitled 65-year-olds demand that daughter-in-law fund their retirement plan, she refuses and puts her own family’s future first: 'They'll be an obligation for the next 20 years'
items.text:
Most couples figure out early on that marriage is essentially two people trying to merge their wildly different upbringings into something functional. But then you end up in a situation that reminds you just how mismatched those family dynamics really are. One woman and her husband built an entire life far away from both of their families; they accomplished everything through a combination of hard work and some financial support from her side of the family. Meanwhile, resources from his side flowed in one specific direction: straight toward the younger brother. Not only that, but they've gotten into the habit of barely communicating.

Now, after 15 quiet years, the in-laws have resurfaced with a stunning proposition: they want to move into a retirement home, and they expect our narrator and her husband to foot the bill, all while preserving their house as a future gift for the already-spoiled brother.

At this point, it's clear that boundaries are non-negotiable. Even when it's family, you and your spouse get to decide what obligations are yours and what obligations are theirs. It might be uncomfortable to have a frank conversation about finances, living arrangements, and expectations, but setting limits now will save years of resentment down the line. Family support is one thing; being taken advantage of is another entirely.

items.title: Nosy Uncle shows up to introverted niece's front door unannounced after moving next door, she blatantly ignores him: 'I feel like my privacy is gone and the point of living alone is ruined'
items.text:
If you identify with being introverted, or you live alone, or you don't like to be bothered by other people then this piece will resonate with some tender points. A young woman and her mother live in a trailer park, but in separate trailers. The young woman is the protagonist, and she really stresses how important it is for her to live alone. She lives alone for a reason, and she likes her peace and quiet. Even though her mom lives right next door, they've developed an agreement that she contacts her over the phone before just randomly showing up.

But everything changes when her uncle joins them. He moves in with the mom to get back on his feet, and that's when things turn ugly. The uncle doesn't have the same understandings about privacy and peace that his niece has. She really doesn't like to be bothered, and he's come knocking on her door. She ignores him, but wonders if it's the right thing to do.

items.title: Dad leaves wife and three children for 11-day trip to the Bahamas, missing daughter's eye surgery to relax on a beach: 'He's making me feel crazy for being mad'
items.text:
Having a partner that seems to forget at the most inconvenient moments that adulthood is team sport is incredibly frustrating. Most of us have learned pretty quickly that marriage and parenting is not about "every man for himself." No, it's about teamwork, and if one goes down, both go down together and fighting. But every now and then, someone randomly reverts to their pre-family brain, and the results are exemplified perfectly in today's tale

One woman's in-laws invited her husband on a family vacation and made it very clear they meant him and his siblings only, as though he's still 17 and not a grown adult with a wife, a job, and no less than three children. He claims he was guilted into saying yes… which might be more sympathetic if the timing didn't coincide with his wife working full-time, solo-parenting for days, and their daughter literally having an important eye surgery.

So now she's overwhelmed, furious, and trying to figure out how her husband could possibly think this was okay. Meanwhile, he's wondering why she's "still mad" three days later. You can probably imagine what the internet commenters are thinking about this one, but scroll down anyway to read it for yourself.

items.title: 25 Hilarious Dad Memes for Wholesome Fathers Flexing Their Funny Bone
items.text:
Fathers around the world, unite in glorious rapture. The nightingale is in full flight, singing songs of morning sorrows that all but the lonesome can hear. Being a father isn't like being any other man. As a parent, it's your civil and personal duty to embolden your children to the best of your abilities. As you imbue the qualities of hard work, reliability, steady, grounded, and even a little chaotic. From sharing moments together in front of the TV on Saturday morning watching cartoons, playing video games on weekends, to cooking together for the whole family, dads come in handy in the most unpredictable ways.

Unlike moms, we love to make dads the back of every joke. They're men, they can handle a little teasing here and there, right? A wholesome father is the head of the family, but as we all know from the infamous movie My Big Fat Greek Wedding, the woman is the neck, and she can turn the head any way she wants.

items.title: 'She cannot be trusted': Wary daughter refuses to give her baby's birth certificate to her mother so she can open a bank account for him, suspects an attempt at fraud
items.text:
Everyone seems to have at least one relative who severely lacks respect or awareness for boundaries. If you don't think you have a family member like that, then I advise you check your family group chats because sometimes the red flags hide in plain sight. Now, we've all heard of entitled people using family members' homes as free hotels or expecting discounts from their artistically talented relatives. While annoying, these are pretty tame instances of boundary-crossing. But what do you do when a family member starts feeling entitled to your official documents?

One woman is dealing with a mom who suddenly wants to open a bank account "for the baby"… except she only wants a picture of the birth certificate, refuses to take no for an answer, and has rallied the siblings to shame her when she pushes back. Never mind that the kid already has a proper savings account set up. Never mind that no legitimate bank is opening accounts off a blurry iPhone snap of a vital document. This mom's reasoning is only looking sketchier by the minute, leading the boy's mom to suspect an attempt at fraud.

items.title: 'Why is he texting you?': Woman refuses to go back to jealous ex after years of possessiveness that drove her away, she regains her confidence and internet supports her strength
items.text:
It can feel so easy and comfortable to go back to an ex. There's something about that familiarity with someone that just comforts all those lonely crevices we all carry. Dating is tough, we all know it. Why put yourself out there for bad first dates, ghosters, and mixed signals when at least with your ex you know the behaviors like the back of your thumb.

But in the story below, this woman does what we all strive to do in those lonely moments when our ex is begging for our return: she says no. It takes a lot of self control and restraint to say no to the pulls of nostalgia. Suddenly you start wondering why you two broke up in the first place. But she kept her head on straight and did remember the bad stuff. His controlling jealousy pushed her away, and kept her away. Read the full story for all the details.

items.title: 20 Animal Memes That Are the Perfect Antidote for Every Gal’s Stressful Day
items.text:
Welcome, gals. Some days are just… a lot. The group chat is popping off about everyone's drama, you can't seem to make any progress on your to-do list despite feeling interminably busy, and your brain has decided to go into overdrive by overthinking. I, myself, am having one those days today, in fact. When the world feels a little too loud and your stress levels start creeping into the red zone, there's only one thing that could possibly help: animals being adorable, dramatic, and unintentionally hilarious.

Whether you need a quick mood boost, a reason to smile between meetings, or a full emotional reset after a crash out, these 20 animal memes are here to rescue your day with pure, unfiltered serotonin. Or you can send them to a friend in need that you know is going through it. Scroll on and let the fluffy, chaotic energy do its magic.

items.title: Parenting Humor: The Funniest Tweets Every Parent Needs to See
items.text:
Welcome, parents. Nothing truly prepares you for raising tiny humans. Not the mountain of parenting books stacked on your nightstand, not the podcasts you binged during late-night feedings, and definitely not the 200 TikToks you saved of that picture-perfect Montessori family who somehow has time to make organic snacks from scratch and practice gentle parenting without breaking a sweat. Maybe you even logged years of babysitting or helped raise siblings, but burping your cousin's newborn or chasing your neighbor's toddler around the yard barely scratches the surface of full-time parenting.

Parenthood is both more magical and more terrifying than you ever imagined. It's the joy of watching a small, brand-new person discover the world with your guidance, mixed with the exhaustion that only a parent can describe. But you're doing your best, and that's more than enough. Scroll down for some hilarious, painfully accurate tweets from parents who fully understand the wild, wonderful ride of raising kids.

items.title: Husband starts claiming wife’s wedding photography work as his own, insists he is part of the creative process by “supporting” her: ‘I didn’t build this career for someone else to take partial credit’
items.text:
In creative fields, there's something really special about your work finally starting to get the recognition you've poured years of sweat, time, and money into. Whether you're a painter, designer, photographer, or writer, your portfolio becomes an extension of you. It's a record of every late night, every risk, every skill sharpened through repetition. So when someone else begins to blur the line between supporting your craft and absorbing credit for it, the situation can get uncomfortable fast. One wedding photographer found herself in exactly that spot when her boyfriend began telling people they were a "creative team," proudly showing off her portfolio as if it were a shared endeavor.

Sometimes things with creative duos can get pretty murky when it comes to determining who the final product belongs to. If I give my husband's script for film class constructive criticism and he completely follows all of my input, is it still just his? If I ask him to mix some green oil paint for me or what figure to draw in a certain spot in my artwork, is my art now partially made by him? But the guy in this story isn't even a photographer. He's just a sales rep that wants to take credit for his wife's work.

items.title: Aunt buys 4-year-old nephew too many toys against parents’ wishes, they accuse her of ruining his birthday by spoiling him
items.text:
Family birthdays can be emotional enough on their own, but when the child being celebrated is a long-awaited miracle baby, the stakes feel even higher. Everyone wants the day to be perfect, meaningful, and full of joy. This sort of pressure can sometimes lead to tension in unexpected places.

One well-meaning aunt recently tried to give her nephew a thoughtful, handmade birthday gift as well as some Lego sets, only to be accused of "ruining" the entire celebration. What was meant to be a sweet gesture became a debate about boundaries, spoiling children, and how much influence extended family members should have over parenting.

My two cents here is that no one should ever give anything to children that their parents don't approve of; it's simply a line that should never be crossed! It doesn't matter how absurd or illogical it may seem to you. The fact that this aunt went against the parents' very clear requests not to bring all these presents just proves to me that the gesture was more for her than it was for the kid.

items.title: 'It's of the utmost importance that he eats quietly': Women explain the weirdest quirks they need their partners to have
items.text:
You know that moment when you realize you are the weird one about something everyone else treats as totally normal? I remember once I was in a group of friends chatting about hobbies and casually said I love organizing my bookshelves by color and size and theme, and they looked at me like I was crazy. The thought of it seemed alien to them! That's when I learned that weirdness is actually relative.

Down below, you will find lots of women opening up about the odd little things they feel strongly about when it comes to a partner. It is a thread of quirks, tastes, and fixations that leave everyone else scratching their heads. These are the sorts of things you only ever confess when you're fairly sure you'll be met with "same!" or "wow, you too?" instead of judgment.

If you've ever found youeself debating whether or not to break up with a guy over a tiny, grating, and niche detail, this one's for you! You might even find some like-minded individuals.

items.title: 21 Lord of the Rings Memes for Middle Earth Couples on a Journey to Mordor This Week
items.text:
Since it's 1954 release by the genius author, J.R.R. Tolkien, it's engrossed not only the hearts and minds of geeky readers still attached to classic literature, but it's only growing in popularity on screen as well. It's not easy to be popular for long periods of time these days: with smartphones warping everyone's attention span, it's surprising that a long, epic like this one has remained so immensely popular. For nerdy couples who prefer a movie night in on a Friday night than the chaos and aesthetic of going out, these memes are for you. There are plenty of Middle Earth Couples simply daydreaming about Frodo and The Shire.

But The Lord of the Rings is more than a fantasy—it's a moral compass. It teaches that even the smallest person can change the course of the future, that true power lies not in power but in mercy, and that hope can endure even in the darkest of times.

items.title: 80s Memes That Will Transport Gen X Ladies Back in Time
items.text:
Remember when childhood meant being completely unreachable for hours at a time? If you grew up in the '80s, you know exactly what that kind of freedom felt like. You'd hop on your bike after breakfast, disappear until dinner, and nobody worried because, well, texting wasn't even a concept yet. It was just you, your friends, and the vague rule of "be home before dark." Back then, there were no filters, no feeds, no doom scrolling, just Polaroids, mixtapes, and the smell of freshly opened VHS tapes at Blockbuster. If you wanted to see your friends, you literally had to go outside.

So whether you miss your Trapper Keeper, your favorite pair of jelly shoes, or just the feeling of being bored with no screen to save you from your own mind, these blasts from the past will take you straight back to the best parts of growing up Gen X.

items.title: Gen X Fashion Trends and Fads No 80s Girl Will Forget: A Fashion Flashback
items.text:
Greetings, Gen X girlies. The 80s weren't all neon spandex and mall bangs… though we definitely had our fair share of both. Thanks to the Stranger Things revival and the unstoppable Y2K nostalgia wave, Gen Z has started digging through our fashion archives again. But while they're busy calling mom jeans "vintage" and pairing scrunchies with claw clips, those of us who actually lived it remember the cozier side of 80s style.

The 80s were the absolute best time to look fashionable in the fall. I'm talking about sweater dresses worn with slouchy boots, ruffled blouses tucked into high-waisted denim, and oversized blazers that look like armor. Honestly, there were too many trends to name, so today, we'll focus on just a handful of some more overlooked fashion fads. So if you're feeling nostalgic for the soft knits, poufy sleeves, and the general aesthetic of it all, this little trip down memory lane should do the trick.

items.title: Woman bans coworker from Secret Santa after unexpected employee showdown over gift exchange rules: 'You either play or you don't'
items.text:
Office Secret Santas are one of those things that sound way more wholesome in theory than they often turn out to be in practice. At their best, they're a cute way to spread a little holiday cheer and laugh over who got a regifted pair of socks from last year. At their worst, they can really devolve into totally unecessary office drama due to debates about fairness.

I've definitely worked places where people took it way too seriously (spreadsheets, budgets, gift guidelines) in an attempt to make sure that everything was fair and square, and yet, someone always wanted to bend the rules "just a little." Usually it's the kind of small thing that shouldn't cause any trouble … and yet somehow does. In this story, one well-meaning coworker's attempt to give without receiving throws the whole Secret Santa system into question. His plight is understandable; he doesn't want to receive a gift because his house already has too much clutter, but he does want to get a gift for someone else. We love a minimalist king, but it does mess up the flow.

items.title: 22 Introvert Memes That Accurately Depict the Desire to be Alone
items.text:
The internet is a wondrous place for introverts; no need to talk to people face to face, to open your mouth and speak, or to make eye contact with anyone. Though people may see your introvertedness as inimical, it's actually just an aversion to socializing for long periods of time. With the invention of the internet, you can spend as much time with yourself as you want.

Extroverts on the other hand, might be so entangled with their need for constant socialization that they can't empathize with the desire to be alone. Regardless of where someone stands, having some peace and quiet to yourself is something everyone should do once in a while. It's important for peace of mind, recharging, and being able to function properly in society. So if you're a quiet introvert looking for some alone time, solo movie nights, and for people to leave you alone, this listicle is for you.

items.title: Nostalgic Cartoon Memes for the '90s Girls Raised by Nickelodeon and Disney
items.text:
Listen, I know this is where I'm supposed to wax poetic about the holy trinity of childhood TV: Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, and Disney Channel. Saturday mornings were sacred, and those three channels basically raised us. But every so often, if the cable gods were feeling generous, I'd stumble onto Discovery Kids, a mysterious, slightly offbeat corner of television that felt like finding a secret level in a video game.

Shows like Tutenstein, Time Warp Trio, and Strange Days at Blake Holsey High completely rewired my little brain. While everyone else was quoting SpongeBob, I was deep in my "ancient Egypt meets quantum physics" era. It was weird, wonderful, and very formative. Seriously, I think those shows are responsible for me being the way that I am. So whether you were a Discovery Kids devotee like me or a pure Nickelodeon loyalist, these cartoon memes will take you right back to that simpler time when your biggest worry was whether your favorite show came on before dinner.

items.title: Wife demands husband limit free time with nehpews after daughters start feeling left behind: 'I never said they weren't good kids'
items.text:
One-on-one time with my parents always felt so special as a kid. They didn't even have to plan anything super involved with me to make is feel important, either. I had my own little rituals with each parent; with my dad, we'd always go to IHOP since my mom wasn't too big on pancakes. And with my mom, we'd go window shopping at the mall. Sometimes she'd buy me something, but she taught me to enjoy perusing. These moments felt so important because it was just me and my parent with no distractions or competition.

But sometimes things aren't so straightforward. It's easy to assume that more kids equal more fun, but anyone who's seen a group of cousins together knows it can quickly turn into a full-blown competition rather than playtime. In this story, one mom found herself torn between empathy for her husband's nephews whose dad is often away for military service and her daughters, who just want to enjoy their dad's attention without feeling like they're in a soccer championship.
